classification.difficultyReason: Sketch positive and negative reciprocal functions and calculate two points on each curve.

content.prompt: Sketch each graph, and indicate two points on each graph.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants I and III; asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$. Two points are $(1,3)$ and $(3,1)$.
answer.worked:
For $x=1$ and $x=3$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{3}{1}\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{3}{3}\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
Plot $(1,3)$ and $(3,1)$. Sketch the two reciprocal branches in quadrants I and III, approaching the axes without meeting them.

spec.description: Complete reciprocal graph with coordinate axes, no grid or numerical ticks, and two labelled points.
spec.mathematics: y=3/x; points (1,3) and (3,1); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants I and III; asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$. Two points are $(1,\tfrac32)$ and $(\tfrac32,1)$.
answer.worked:
For $x=1$ and $x=\frac32$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{3}{2(1)}\\y&=\frac32\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{3}{2(\frac32)}\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
Plot $(1,\frac32)$ and $(\frac32,1)$. Sketch the two reciprocal branches in quadrants I and III, approaching the axes without meeting them.

spec.description: Complete reciprocal graph with two labelled points; a leader separates the lower point label from the nearby curve.
spec.mathematics: y=3/(2x); points (1,3/2) and (3/2,1); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants II and IV; asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$. Two points are $(-1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$.
answer.worked:
For $x=-1$ and $x=1$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac{1}{-1}\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac{1}{1}\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
Reflect $y=\frac1x$ in the $x$-axis. Plot $(-1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$, and sketch the branches in quadrants II and IV, approaching the axes without meeting them.

spec.description: Reflected basic hyperbola with branches in quadrants II and IV and two labelled points.
spec.mathematics: y=-1/x; points (-1,1) and (1,-1); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants II and IV; asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$. Two points are $(-1,3)$ and $(1,-3)$.
answer.worked:
For $x=-1$ and $x=1$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac{3}{-1}\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac{3}{1}\\y&=-3\end{align*}$$
Stretch $y=\frac1x$ by a factor of 3 from the $x$-axis and reflect it in the $x$-axis. Plot $(-1,3)$ and $(1,-3)$, and sketch the branches in quadrants II and IV, approaching the axes without meeting them.

spec.description: Negative reciprocal graph with coordinate axes and two labelled points.
spec.mathematics: y=-3/x; points (-1,3) and (1,-3); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.
